extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal authors, peer reviewers, and research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and constraints for use, disclosure, and reviewer handling of generative AI in research manuscripts, grant proposals, and peer review across federal agencies and major journals/publishers. Covers where to disclose, what is prohibited (authorship, images, reviewer use), enforcement, and discipline-specific nuances.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI authorship prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: No major journal or agency allows AI to be listed as an author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policies cite accountability requirements that only humans can fulfill; AI must not be credited as an author across federal agencies and major publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure location: acknowledgments and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Most require disclosure in acknowledgments sections, with research-specific AI use detailed in methods sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General-purpose AI use (e.g., copy editing) is commonly disclosed in acknowledgments; AI used for data processing, analysis, or experimental design should be described in Methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt and prompt-disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Some policies (e.g., Science/AAAS) require full prompt disclosure in acknowledgments and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When required, include the prompts and details of how the LLM was used; failure to disclose prompt-derived content may be treated as misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review restrictions (no uploading/manuscript sharing to AI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nearly universal prohibition on uploading manuscripts or confidential review material to AI tools due to confidentiality concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers must not submit peer review material to general online AI tools; agencies/journals may also ban any reviewer use of non-approved AI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer-use declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Some journals require reviewers to declare any use of AI tools transparently (e.g., Nature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer uses an approved AI tool (where permitted), they must disclose that use to editors/relevant channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human author responsibility and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: Human authors remain fully accountable for the accuracy and integrity of AI-generated content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must verify and fact-check any AI-assisted text or outputs; policies emphasize author responsibility for errors, plagiarism, and integrity of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH-specific restrictions on reviewer AI use
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH policy (NOT-OD-23-149) specifically bars natural language processors and large language models from peer review processes, citing confidentiality violations when grant content is uploaded to online AI tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to grant peer review; uploading application content to external AI tools is prohibited and treated as a confidentiality breach.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF guidance on disclosure and reviewer restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF encourages researchers to indicate AI use in project descriptions while prohibiting reviewers from using non-approved AI tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers should disclose AI use in proposals; reviewers must avoid non-approved AI tools—formalization expected in policies (e.g., PAPPG 2025).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funder baseline: DOD lack of research disclosure rules
rubrics_metrics.description: DOD focuses on operational AI development guidelines and lacks specific research disclosure requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers funded by DOD should consult program-specific guidance; no general DOD research-disclosure standard was identified.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-impact journal strictness (Science/AAAS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Science implements a complete ban on AI-generated text and treats violations as scientific misconduct; requires full prompt disclosure where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations can be escalated as misconduct; Science's stance represents the most restrictive approach and may set de facto standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature: middle-ground rules for LLM and images
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature prohibits AI authorship and AI-generated images while allowing some AI assistance for copy editing without disclosure; requires reviewer declaration of AI use due to confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copy editing assistance may be exempt from disclosure; any substantive AI use (analysis, generation) must be documented in Methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: JAMA: automated screening and institutional review considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: JAMA requires detailed reporting in Acknowledgments/Methods and uses automated submission screening; includes institutional review board considerations for AI use in research design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare for automated checks for AI-generated text and include IRB/ethical oversight details when AI affects study design or participant data.

rubrics_metrics.name: IEEE: acknowledgment disclosure and recommended grammar-editing disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: IEEE requires disclosure in Acknowledgments with AI system identification and recommends disclosing grammar editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All IEEE journals follow consistent portfolio-wide policy: prohibit AI authorship, require identification of the AI system used.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-generated images: bans and caption requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Many publishers ban AI-generated or modified images (APS/Physical Review) or require caption descriptions for AI-generated graphics (ACS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If AI-produced graphics are permitted (rare), explicitly label them in captions and provide generation details; otherwise, do not submit AI-generated/modified images.

rubrics_metrics.name: PLOS: comprehensive Methods/Acknowledgments disclosure and tool evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS requires comprehensive disclosure in Methods and Acknowledgments with detailed evaluation descriptions of the tools used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document how the AI tool was evaluated (accuracy, limitations) and include that evaluation in Methods; disclose tool name/version in Acknowledgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cell Press: readability-only use and standardized disclosure template
rubrics_metrics.description: Cell Press restricts AI to readability/language improvements and uses a standardized disclosure template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substantive content generation is disallowed; use provided template to disclose permitted language-polishing assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher-wide portfolio standards (Elsevier, Springer Nature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Large publishers implement cross-portfolio policies distinguishing copy-editing exemptions from generative AI requiring disclosure; Elsevier generally mandates disclosure and limits AI-generated images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow publisher-level policies which may apply to many journals; check journal-specific additions to publisher rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline-specific norms: social sciences and humanities caution
rubrics_metrics.description: Humanities and social science journals are more cautious; some (AJPS) require disclosure and discourage AI for substantial elements such as literature reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid using AI for interpretive, contextual, or creative tasks central to scholarship; disclose even limited uses and follow field-specific expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and submission disclosure requirements (PMLA, AJPS, AER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some journals require full citation of AI-created content at submission (PMLA), disclosure in text/footnotes plus author questionnaire (AJPS), or brief submission disclosure for drafting/editing with fact-checking obligations (AER).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the journal's specified location and format for disclosure (manuscript, footnotes, questionnaire, or submission metadata); be prepared to document the scope of AI involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover letter/editor notification for disclosure (APS/Physical Review)
rubrics_metrics.description: APS (Physical Review) asks for disclosure to editors in the cover letter and limits AI to light editing only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting to Physical Review journals, disclose any permitted AI use in the cover letter and avoid AI-generated/modified images.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement mechanisms: screening and misconduct classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies use enforcement mechanisms including automated screening, editorial checks, and classifying serious violations as scientific misconduct (Science).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect submissions to be checked automatically; undisclosed or deceptive AI use may trigger investigations and sanctions under misconduct policies.
